source_title: Indian sports wrap, October 27: Injured para-cyclist Arshad Shaikh undergoes surgery - Sportstar
source_excerpt: PARA CYCLING Indian para-cyclist Arshad Shaikh, who injured himself grievously after suffering a fall during the recent Aichi-Nagoya Asian Para Games, has undergone a surgery in Shizouka and is recovering well, the Sports Authority of India (SAI) said on Tuesday. Shaikh suffered the fall during the men’s time trial event at the Games. He is currently recuperating at the Chutoen General Medical Centre in Shizuoka Prefecture, Japan. “The Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports (MYAS) and the Sports Authority of India (SAI) are in constant touch with the athlete and the Indian Embassy in Japan and are coordinating all possible assistance required by Arshad,” the SAI stated. Shaikh suffered a fracture in his left residual limb due to the fall. He was the country’s lone competitor in the cycling competition of the Asian Para Games, where India won a record-breaking 114 medals, including 30 gold. The Indian embassy in Japan also posted pictures of Shaikh after he was paid a visit by the country’s ambassador Nagma Mohammed Mallick on Monday. “The Ambassador expressed hopes for the athlete’s speedy recovery and conveyed to team members that the Indian Embassy would continue to provide support until he reaches a health condition allowing his return to India,” stated the embassy. “Ambassador wished him a speedy recovery and assured his team of the Embassy’s continued support until he is medically fit to travel back to India,” it added. Shaikh hails from Andhra Pradesh and represented India in the Paris Olympics. -PTI BADMINTON Meghana in women’s singles, Achutaditya-Arjun men’s doubles pair fail to make Hylo Open main draw Indian women’s singles player Meghana Reddy Mareddy and the men’s doubles pair of Achutaditya Rao Doddavarapu and Arjun Reddy Pochana failed to reach the main draw of the USD 500,000 Hylo Open Super 500 badminton tournament after losing their respective qualifying round matches in Saarbrucken on Tuesday. Meghana lost to Ranithma Liyanage of Sri Lanka 9-21 10-21 in 27 minutes, while the Achutaditya-Arjun duo went down fighting 9-21 22-20 11-21 to Switzerland’s Yann Orteu and Minh Quang Pham in a match that lasted 50 minutes. Two-time Olympic medallist P V Sindhu, who had finished runner-up at the French Open last week, takes on Turkey’s Neslihan Arin in the women’s singles opening round. Ashmita Chaliha, Devika Sihag, Aakarshi Kashyap, Malvika Bansod and Unnati Hooda will also be competing in the women’s singles main draw. Lakshya Sen, H S Prannoy, Kiran George and Tharun Mannepalli will compete in the men’s singles. -PTI MORE SPORTS Somaiya Vidyavihar University, Sheffield Hallam University join hands to advance sports and exercise science Somaiya Vidyavihar University (SVU) and the UK's Sheffield Hallam University have signed a two-year Memorandum of Understanding (MoU), with the support of Oliver Coppard, Mayor of South Yorkshire, to explore academic collaboration in sports and exercise science. The partnership will explore joint research, staff and student exchange, the progression and joint development of academic programmes, and other scholarly endeavours. SVU’s commitment to sport includes hosting the FISU World University Championship Squash in 2026. Its academic programmes in sports and exercise science aim to connect scientific learning with practical sporting experiences, creating opportunities for students pursuing careers in sport. Sheffield Hallam University brings expertise in sport, physical activity, human performance and sports management. Prof. Ajay Kapoor, vice-chancellor of Somaiya Vidyavihar University, said, “Understanding human performance requires more than what we see on the field; it requires scientific research that can translate into better outcomes in sport, health and wellbeing.” -Team Sportstar CRICKET 10th National T20 Championship for Deaf begins in Surat The 10th National T20 Championship for Deaf, being organised by the Indian Deaf Cricket Association (IDCA) in Surat, features 14 teams. The championship began on Monday and will run until November 1. The matches are being held at Bawaji Cricket Ground, and teams from Andhra Pradesh, Haryana, Mumbai, Vidarbha, Rajasthan, Chhattisgarh, Kerala, Delhi, Chandigarh, Jammu and Kashmir, Tamil Nadu, Karnataka, Gujarat and Uttar Pradesh are participating this time. -Team Sportstar SQUASH Sub-Junior/ Junior National Squash: Shiven, Riyansika advance to semis with five-game wins Tamil Nadu’s Shiven Agarwal and Karnataka’s Riyansika Verma recorded thrilling five-game victories over 3/4 seeds Shresht Iyer and Fabiha Nafees in the U-17 boys and girls quarterfinals respectively in the Sub-Junior & Junior National Squash Championship in Jaipur on Tuesday. Seeded 5/8, Agarwal came from behind to defeat Karnataka’s Iyer 8-11, 11-5, 11-6, 10-12, 11-6. In the girls draw, Riyansika (5/8) recovered from a 2-1 deficit to get past Uttar Pradesh’s Fabiha 11-4, 9-11, 7-11, 11-6, 11-9. There was another upset in the U-19 boys section, where Rajasthan’s Subhash Choudhary (5/8) beat 3/4 seed Raghav Vashistha of Uttar Pradesh 11-5, 11-7, 11-6 to book a place in the semifinals. The tournament is spread across 10 categories, and the finals will be held on Thursday -Team Sportstar
